structure: Saturn V S-II stage common bulkhead (LOX tank aft/top dome shared with LH2 tank bottom), North American Aviation, Seal Beach CA
dome_or_shell_shape: Modified ellipsoidal dome, about 33 ft diameter and 12 ft high each; compound contour of three sections (elliptical, toroidal, conical); each facing sheet built from 12 gore panels plus a 3-ft 'dollar' cap; core surface area about 1400 sq ft. (10.06 m is my conversion of 33 ft; SP-4206 says 10 m.)

construction.faces: 2014-T6 aluminium aft and forward facing sheets; gores chemically milled, tapering from about 13 mm (1/2 in) at base to 0.79 mm (1/32 in) at apex (SP-4206 p.214, NAA brochure). No separate uniform face-sheet gauge is given in any source opened.
construction.core: Phenolic honeycomb; SP-4206 and RPE call it fiberglass/phenolic, SD 71-256 p.4-48 calls it 'phenolic impregnated nylon' (sources disagree); thickness from nearly 5 in (about 13 cm) at apex to 0.080 in (RPE) or about 1/8 in (NAA brochure) at the periphery; cells 3/8 by 4.75 in per SD 71-256 p.1-26 (wording unclear); core pre-faced and supplied as blocks/panels (Honeycomb Products per NAA brochure)
construction.adhesive: HT 424 pre-bond primer named (NAA brochure); adhesive film type for S-II not stated in sources opened (HT 424 adhesive is named for the Douglas S-IV/S-IVB bulkheads in Douglas Paper 3817). Bondline-bridging limit about 0.010 in (SD 71-256).
construction.overall: Gore forming: 10 x 22 ft gores, underwater explosive forming (3 blasts per gore) at El Toro using pits up to 25 ft diameter by 15 ft deep with 80-ton crane (SD 71-256 p.4-50; SP-4206 p.213)

tooling: No hard bonding mold: skins are inflated (aft sheet at 1/2 psi air, tool seals the underside) and measured; forward sheet drawn smooth under a compartmented vacuum bell, then lowered onto the core by overhead crane and vacuum bell and pulled down by 130 turnbuckle-type load cells to 1000 lb each. 43 dial indicators on a 'rainbow beam' measure contour every 2 degrees of circumference. Core machined on a skate-mounted cutter (diamond-coated, 8-in diameter, face concave to the 198-in radius) following computer cutting tables. 636 bolts later join J-section to LH2 tank (SP-4206).

cure_method.process: Adhesive bonded in an autoclave ('gargantuan autoclave' per SP-4206 p.213) for the core-to-aft-sheet bond; skins bonded to core 'in a condition of preload induced by applications of vacuum and/or pressure' (NAA brochure). Whether the final forward-sheet bond is also autoclaved is not stated in the S-II sources opened (it is for the S-IVB).
cure_method.facility: Autoclave size not found in any source opened (null). Assembly building and bulkhead fabrication building at Seal Beach mentioned only in film captions (not opened).

assembly: 12 gores welded (20-ft meridian welds) into each facing sheet, plus dollar; aft sheet loaded on tool; core panels fit to measured contour, bonded to aft sheet, then machined in 0.010-in increments per 360-degree pass around the panel periphery until the core contour matches the forward sheet contour; forward sheet lowered on and bonded. Sequence: weld -> chemical clean/prime HT 424 -> measure (about 15,000 points total) -> machine core -> PVC-film impression fit check -> bond. Circumference of welded bulkheads held to a tolerance via Pi-tape checks after every second meridian weld.

shape_accuracy.quote: the core contour must match the bulkhead within ten thousandths of an inch
shape_accuracy.location: SD 71-256 printed p.4-45 (PDF p.296); NAA brochure says 'within the required 10,000ths of an inch' (ambiguous wording; SD 71-256 equates it to 0.010 in)

shape_accuracy.quantity: core fit check before adhesive, via PVC impression layer
shape_accuracy.quote: verifies that the core matches the facing sheet within 0.010 inch

shape_accuracy.quote: the maximum gap which the adhesive can bridge

Cutting machine head is re-adjusted for the next 0.010-inch cut

shape_accuracy.quote: tolerance of +-0.078 inch (which is theoretically +-0.025 inch on the diameter)
shape_accuracy.location: SD 71-256 p.4-47 (PDF p.298); OCR renders +- as '*'; stated to be hard to hold

shape_accuracy.quantity: calculated cutter profile error in the 198-in-radius region
shape_accuracy.quote: theoretical error of less than 0.0015 inch

shape_accuracy.value: 0.011 on 20-ft welds; mismatch over 0.028 judged too large on the forward-bulkhead-to-cylinder weld

inspection: Ultrasonic through-transmission (primary) plus pulse-echo (supplement on lower 15 in where core is thin), recorded on a C-scan; water squirter nozzles, turntable at 3 rpm with 0.060 in index per revolution; suspect areas checked by sonic methods, radiography if canted core suspected; out-of-tolerance debonds go to Material Review Board (SD 70-556-1 pp.131-161). SP-4206 p.214: ultrasonic equipment verified complete bonding. Photoelastic coating was proposed to inspect the 33-ft bulkhead in hours instead of days (NTRS 19660024836). NO flaw counts, void sizes or disbond frequencies for S-II bulkheads found in any source opened.
problems: Thin gores sag, so core fit was among the 'most critical operations' (SP-4206 p.214); localized distortion from residual stress (SD 71-256); first approach (putty pads, about 1700 measurements) judged inadequate and replaced by inflation technique; phenolic dust from machining hurt bonding (SD 71-256 p.2-33); heat leak through bulkhead cells higher than predicted, fixed by vacuum pumping (p.1-26). Secondary sources only: first aft bulkhead ruptured at a repaired weld in hydrostatic proof test 28 Oct 1964; a bulkhead burst in a water test days before shipment in 1965 (hslb.org page fetched, not archived); no error-free bulkhead-to-cylinder weld until Jan 1968.
cost_class: No dollar figures found. Qualitative: NAA brochure says the inflation technique 'reduces manufacturing costs by eliminating the need for hard tooling'; hand sanding judged not acceptable at S-II size (SD 71-256); schedule slips noted in secondary sources only.

structure: Saturn S-IVB (and S-IV) common bulkhead, Douglas Aircraft, Huntington Beach
dome_or_shell_shape: Hemispherical/spherical double-faced dome, about 5 cm thick (SP-4206 p.167); Douglas Paper 3817 p.3: 'spherical in shape', S-IV and S-IVB differ only in diameter and thickness. Welded gore segments plus dollar and attach rings. (S-IVB 21.7 ft is the task's figure; 6.63 m is SP-4206's.)

construction.faces: 2014-T6 aluminium; forward sheet 0.813 mm, aft sheet 1.4 mm (SP-4206 p.167). Experimental S-IV article used nominal 0.025 in (0.64 mm) LH2 skin (Douglas p.7).
construction.core: Phenolic fiberglass honeycomb (HRP core); experimental article used 6 lb/cu ft core in a 12-in band at the greatest circumference and 4 lb/cu ft elsewhere (Douglas p.8)
construction.adhesive: HT 424 primer and HT 424 adhesive film (Douglas p.8)

tooling: Aft dome set on a bonding fixture; honeycomb bonded to it; forward dome lowered over fixture for final bond; contour mismatch measured with the 'Paulino/Paleno block' system: 350 small honeycomb blocks, each with a putty pad, forward dome lowered on to record indentation (SP-4206 pp.167-168; Douglas p.4); final core surface spot-faced then hand sanded; finished unit machined on a Niles boring mill (SP-4206 p.168).

cure_method.process: Autoclave, vacuum bag, two bond cycles (core to aft dome; then forward dome to core)
cure_method.temperature: 182 C (360 F) final bond cycle (SP-4206 p.168); 325 F in the experimental S-IV article (Douglas p.8)
cure_method.pressure: 45 psi (310 kPa, my conversion) under vacuum bag, experimental article (Douglas p.8)
cure_method.facility: 'oversized autoclave' (SP-4206 p.168); size not given. Cycle durations: first bond about 30 h including heat-up and cool-down with thermocouple spread held to 10 F; integral forward-dome bond needs 60 h with 5 F spread because both domes must contract together (Douglas pp.9-10).

assembly: Preformed gore segments welded (MIG) into complete forward and aft domes with dollar and attach rings; aft dome on fixture; core bonded (cycle 1); core sculpted; forward dome bonded (cycle 2); machined to tolerance; Douglas (p.5) lists weld porosity, weld cracking, skin debonding and skin wrinkling as the main difficulties, and notes weld metal ages through repeated bond cycles.

shape_accuracy.quantity: gap tolerance between welded gore segments (S-IV)
shape_accuracy.quote: The gap tolerance (between parts) on the S-IV welded segments is 0 to 0.015 in.

shape_accuracy.quantity: gap tolerance between bonded gore segments (experimental S-IV)
shape_accuracy.quote: gap tolerance on the bonded segments is 0 to 0.090 in

shape_accuracy.measured_or_specified: measured via 350 putty pads but values not published
shape_accuracy.quote: the aluminum skin developed an exasperatingly uneven terrain of gaps, gullies, and wrinkles

inspection: Sonic (Growler) tests of the core bonds in the experimental S-IV bulkhead found no unbonds ('none were detected'); ultrasonic pulse-echo of bonded doublers found about 80 small unbond areas, each under 1/2 in diameter, mostly overstated by transducer size; small adhesive channels missed by ultrasonics (Douglas pp.12-13). Production inspection statistics not given.
problems: Douglas p.5: weld cracking or debonding has occurred during cryogenic loading in most S-IV common bulkheads; wrinkles on LH2 side of S-IV-6 and the dynamic vehicle attributed to forcing excess forward-dome metal onto the core; Douglas calls fitup and weld-zone cracks 'inherent' to the process; hand sanding 'time consuming and subject to some human error'.
cost_class: Experimental bonded bulkhead used about 50% of the bonding man-hours of a production bulkhead (Douglas Paper 3817 conclusions); no dollar figures.
